description: v0.43 形成终点上的陌生 sender/receiver 社会学习与协议恢复
research_question: 独立形成的协议在陌生主体加入后，能否仅凭共同后果反馈恢复；角色对称性和伙伴覆盖如何改变恢复速度与最终公共性？

factorial.resident_cultures: static/random role order × fixed A, rotating A/B, random A/B/C formation

social_learning.newcomer: identity 0 communication modules freshly reset; private visual frontend inherited from the same visual group
social_learning.trainable: newcomer sender and receiver communication modules only
social_learning.residents: communication and private visual modules frozen
social_learning.role_mode: same role mode as resident culture

measures.endpoint_baseline: v0.44 zero-adaptation compatibility and v0.43 native resident endpoint
measures.interpretation: recovery after feedback is social learning; it is not evidence for open-ended language by itself

hypotheses: A freshly reset newcomer should start near the zero-adaptation mixed-culture baseline and recover function through shared reward.
Residents formed with random role order should yield lower role spread and more stable newcomer recovery across role permutations.
Broad random partner scheduling should recover more transferable structure than a fixed partner schedule, but may require more updates.
controls_and_limits: This first adaptation batch fixes the post-replacement schedule to random A/B/C to isolate resident-culture effects.
The newcomer shares the resident visual frontend family; perception learning and new visual agents are deferred.
The task remains the finite six-site, three-resource, two-token grounded protocol inherited from v0.43.
All residents and the newcomer are trained with the centralized shared reward; no asynchronous communication channel is introduced.
